title: Cataract surgery
what: Through a tiny cut, the surgeon removes the cloudy lens of the eye and puts in an artificial lens. Usually the eye is numbed with drops. General anesthesia is rarely needed.
why: When the lens has become cloudy and your vision gets in the way of daily life: reading and driving are hard, everything looks foggy, and lights cause glare.
duration: surgery usually takes 15 to 30 minutes; you are at the clinic a few hours and usually go home the same day
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. The doctor will tell you what to do
Prostate medicines. They affect the pupil during surgery
Diabetes, high blood pressure, or heart disease
Other eye diseases and past eye surgery

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Before surgery, your eye is measured in detail to choose the lens. Your clinic will give you the list of blood tests and an ECG.

prepare.title: Drops
prepare.text: Sometimes eye drops are prescribed a few days before. Use them as your doctor says.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually a light breakfast is fine. If you will have sedation, do not eat for a few hours. Check with your clinic.

prepare.title: On the day of surgery
prepare.text: Wash your face. Do not use makeup or face cream.

bring: Someone to go with you. You cannot drive after surgery
steps: Drops are put in to widen the pupil and numb the eye
In the operating room, your face is covered with a sterile cloth, with only the eye open
Your eyelids are gently held open, and you look at a light
Through a tiny cut, the surgeon breaks up the cloudy lens and removes it
A soft artificial lens is put in its place
The cut usually seals by itself, and a protective shield is put on the eye
feel: Usually there is no pain. You may feel pressure and coolness
You see light and spots, but not the tools
Afterwards, a gritty feeling in the eye and watering for a day or two
after: Use the eye drops exactly as your doctor says, usually for a few weeks
Do not rub or press on your eye
At first, wear the protective shield at night
Do not lift heavy things or bend down suddenly until your doctor says you can
Keep water, soap, and dust out of the eye for the first days
A checkup is usually the next day. Vision gets better over a few days
red_flags: Severe eye pain that painkillers do not help
Redness or swelling that gets worse, or pus
Flashes, many floaters, or a shadow like a curtain over your eye: see a doctor right away

faq.a: Usually not. The eye is numbed with drops. You may only feel pressure.

faq.q: When can I watch TV and read?
faq.a: Usually by the next day, if your eye feels comfortable. Your doctor will tell you about any limits.
The cataract itself cannot. But sometimes, years later, the membrane behind the lens turns cloudy. A laser clears it in a few minutes.

reminders.text: Eye surgery tomorrow. Use your drops as planned. Arrange for someone to go with you. You cannot drive after surgery.
